faqs.q: In what month and year did Gandhi finally decide to withdraw the civil disobedience movement?

Consider the following statements about British policy considerations after the second Round Table Conference:
(I) Gandhi would not be permitted to build up momentum for another mass movement.
(II) The confidence of loyalists and government functionaries, rather than Congress goodwill, was seen as essential.
(III) The national movement would be encouraged to consolidate in rural areas.
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Statement III is incorrect — British policy aimed to prevent the national movement from consolidating in rural areas, not encourage it.

faqs.q: What group was singled out as facing particularly harsh repression during the resumed civil disobedience phase?
On what date was the Communal Award announced by British PM Ramsay MacDonald?
On what body's findings was the Communal Award based?
How many reserved seats were granted to the depressed classes under the Communal Award?

Consider the following statements about the communities granted separate electorates under the Communal Award:
(I) Muslims, Europeans, and Sikhs.
(II) Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, and depressed classes.
(III) Even Marathas for some seats in Bombay.
Which of the above is/are correct?
Before the Communal Award, what stand had Ambedkar taken in his testimony to the Simon Commission regarding the depressed classes?

options.b: They should be treated as a distinct, independent minority separate from caste Hindus
options.c: They should be merged fully with caste Hindus
options.d: They should be represented only through Congress

faqs.a: They should be treated as a distinct, independent minority separate from caste Hindus

faqs.q: What proposal did the Simon Commission reject regarding the depressed classes, while still retaining a different concept?

options.a: It rejected both reserved seats and separate electorates
options.b: It rejected reserved seats but retained separate electorates
options.c: It rejected separate electorates but retained the concept of reserving seats
options.d: It rejected adult franchise but retained separate electorates

faqs.a: It rejected separate electorates but retained the concept of reserving seats

faqs.q: At the second Round Table Conference, what compromise did Ambedkar attempt with Gandhi before the Communal Award was announced?

options.a: Reserved seats in a common electorate
options.c: Joint electorates with no reservations at all
options.d: A separate constitution for depressed classes

faqs.a: Reserved seats in a common electorate
faqs.e: Gandhi rejected this proposal, having declared himself the sole representative of India's oppressed masses.

faqs.q: Who offered to mediate on the minorities question, on the condition that other committee members supported his decision, leading to the Communal Award?
For how many years was the separate electorate arrangement for the depressed classes to apply, under the Communal Award?
What percentage of seats were to be reserved for women in all provinces except the NWFP, under the Communal Award?
What unique voting arrangement did the Communal Award grant the depressed classes?

options.a: A 'double vote' — one through separate electorates, one through general electorates
options.b: A single vote through separate electorates only
options.c: Proxy voting through caste Hindu representatives

faqs.a: A 'double vote' — one through separate electorates, one through general electorates

faqs.q: How many seats were allocated for the Marathas in the province of Bombay under the Communal Award?
What was the Congress's official stand on the Communal Award?

options.a: Full rejection and demand for its withdrawal
options.c: Strong disagreement, but neither accepting nor rejecting it without minority consent

faqs.a: Strong disagreement, but neither accepting nor rejecting it without minority consent

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's objections to the Communal Award:
(I) He saw it as an attack on Indian unity and nationalism.
(II) He believed separate electorates would undermine the goal of abolishing untouchability.
(III) He believed the Award adequately addressed the socially degraded position of the depressed classes.
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Statement III is incorrect — Gandhi believed the Award provided no answer to the socially degraded position of the depressed classes.

faqs.q: On what date did Gandhi begin his indefinite fast against the Communal Award's separate electorates?

Consider the following statements regarding Gandhi's demand ahead of his fast:
(I) He demanded that the depressed classes be elected through a joint, wider electorate under universal franchise.
(II) He expressed no objection to a larger number of reserved seats for the depressed classes.
Which of the above is/are correct?
Besides Ambedkar, which other leaders helped hammer out the compromise contained in the Poona Pact?

options.b: M.C. Rajah and Madan Mohan Malaviya

faqs.a: M.C. Rajah and Madan Mohan Malaviya

faqs.q: On what date was the Poona Pact signed by Ambedkar on behalf of the depressed classes?
What did the Poona Pact abandon, in exchange for increased reserved seats for the depressed classes?

options.b: The idea of reserved seats altogether
options.c: The idea of separate electorates for the depressed classes

faqs.a: The idea of separate electorates for the depressed classes

faqs.q: By how much did the Poona Pact increase the reserved seats for depressed classes in provincial legislatures?
What share of seats in the Central Legislature did the Poona Pact reserve for the depressed classes?
How did the government treat the Poona Pact in relation to the Communal Award?

options.b: As a complete rejection of the Award
options.c: As an amendment to the Communal Award
options.d: It refused to recognise the Pact

faqs.a: As an amendment to the Communal Award

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements about the impact of the Poona Pact on depressed classes:
(I) It made the depressed classes political tools usable by majoritarian caste Hindu organisations.
(II) It enabled genuine, independent leadership to develop unimpeded among depressed classes.
(III) It subordinated the depressed classes into the Hindu social order by denying them a separate and distinct existence.
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Statement II is incorrect — the Pact is described as making the depressed classes leaderless, since true representatives struggled against caste-Hindu-backed stooges.

faqs.q: What long-term constitutional consequence is attributed to the Poona Pact's denial of a separate identity for Dalits?

options.a: It had no bearing on the later Constitution
options.b: It guaranteed extensive rights in independent India's Constitution
options.c: It led to immediate abolition of untouchability
options.d: It pre-empted rights and safeguards for Dalits in the Constitution of independent India

faqs.a: It pre-empted rights and safeguards for Dalits in the Constitution of independent India

faqs.q: What did the All India Scheduled Caste Federation allege about the joint electorate system under the Government of India Act, 1935?

options.a: It had no effect on representation
options.c: It let the Hindu majority effectively nominate compliant scheduled caste representatives
options.d: It gave scheduled castes full autonomy

faqs.a: It let the Hindu majority effectively nominate compliant scheduled caste representatives

faqs.q: Until what year did Ambedkar continue to denounce the Poona Pact, despite having signed it?
In which month, while still in jail, did Gandhi set up the All India Anti-Untouchability League?
In which month did Gandhi start the weekly publication 'Harijan'?
After his release from jail in August 1933, to which ashram did Gandhi shift, having vowed not to return to Sabarmati Ashram until swaraj was won?
Over what period did Gandhi conduct his Harijan tour of the country, covering about 20,000 km?
What organisation did Gandhi's Harijan tour collect money for?
On which two dates in 1934 did Gandhi undertake fasts to convince followers of the seriousness of his anti-untouchability effort?
What bill did the government defeat in August 1934, seen as the government obliging orthodox and reactionary elements?
What was Gandhi's key call regarding temples, as part of his Harijan campaign?

options.a: Throwing open temples to the untouchables
options.c: Closing all temples until untouchability ended
options.d: Building new temples exclusively for Harijans

faqs.a: Throwing open temples to the untouchables

faqs.q: What did Gandhi call on caste Hindus to do, as part of his campaign, for the miseries inflicted on Harijans?
What was Gandhi's stated view connecting Hinduism and untouchability?

options.b: "Untouchability must be preserved for social order."
options.d: "Hinduism dies if untouchability lives, untouchability has to die if Hinduism is to live."

faqs.a: "Hinduism dies if untouchability lives, untouchability has to die if Hinduism is to live."

faqs.q: Why did Gandhi avoid mixing the issue of removing untouchability with inter-caste marriage and inter-dining?

options.a: He believed marriage reform was more urgent
options.b: He had no view on the matter
options.c: He believed those restrictions existed among Harijans too, and the campaign was specifically directed at disabilities unique to Harijans
options.d: He supported inter-caste restrictions on principle

faqs.a: He believed those restrictions existed among Harijans too, and the campaign was specifically directed at disabilities unique to Harijans

faqs.q: How did Gandhi distinguish between untouchability and the caste system (varnashram) itself?

options.a: He saw untouchability as sinful, but held that the varnashram system itself was not inherently sinful
options.b: He saw no distinction between the two
options.c: He saw the caste system as sinful but untouchability as harmless
options.d: He saw both as equally sinful and sought abolition of both

faqs.a: He saw untouchability as sinful, but held that the varnashram system itself was not inherently sinful

faqs.q: What did Gandhi believe untouchability was a product of, rather than of the caste system itself?
What approach did Gandhi favour toward orthodox Hindus (whom he called 'sanatanis') regarding untouchability, rather than compulsion?

options.a: Persuasion, appealing to their reason and their hearts

faqs.a: Persuasion, appealing to their reason and their hearts

faqs.q: What symbolic parallel is drawn between Gandhi's burning of foreign cloth and Ambedkar's burning of which text?
faqs.e: Both acts represented resistance to bondage and slavery, alongside other symbolic acts like a pinch of salt from the ocean and a drop of water from the Mahad tank.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements comparing Gandhi's and Ambedkar's views on freedom:
(I) Gandhi believed freedom must be wrested from authority by the people who desire it.
(II) Ambedkar expected freedom to be bestowed by the imperial rulers.
Which of the above is/are correct?
Which leader advocated the parliamentary system of government for independent India, while the other had little respect for it?

options.a: Ambedkar advocated it; Gandhi had little respect for it
options.b: Gandhi advocated it; Ambedkar had little respect for it

faqs.a: Ambedkar advocated it; Gandhi had little respect for it

faqs.q: What did Gandhi believe democracy tends to get converted into, given a propensity for domination by leaders?
faqs.e: Ambedkar, by contrast, was inclined towards mass democracy as a pressure tool for the advancement of oppressed people.

faqs.q: What was the one uncompromising principle Gandhi held to, despite having no rigidities of ideology otherwise?
In 'Hind Swaraj', what did Gandhi argue regarding India's status as a nation prior to imperial rule?

options.a: India had always been a nation, and British rule broke its cultural unity
options.c: India's unity was solely a product of British legal systems
options.d: India was never a unified nation before British rule

faqs.a: India had always been a nation, and British rule broke its cultural unity
faqs.e: Ambedkar held the opposite view — that Indian unity was a by-product of the legal system introduced by the imperial state.

faqs.q: What did 'Gramraj' (village self-rule) represent for Gandhi, in contrast to Ambedkar's view of Indian villages?

options.a: For Gandhi, Gramraj was real independence ('Ramraj'); Ambedkar saw villages as denying equality, fraternity and liberty
options.c: For Gandhi, villages were sites of oppression; for Ambedkar, they were ideal
options.d: Both rejected the village system entirely

faqs.a: For Gandhi, Gramraj was real independence ('Ramraj'); Ambedkar saw villages as denying equality, fraternity and liberty

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's and Ambedkar's views on machinery and mechanisation:
(I) Gandhi was apprehensive about mechanisation's de-humanising and exploitative impact.
(II) Ambedkar attributed machinery's evil effects to wrong social organisation, not machinery itself, and believed it benefited all.
Which of the above is/are correct?
How did Ambedkar's and Gandhi's notions of non-violence differ?

options.b: Ambedkar was an absolute pacifist; Gandhi accepted relative violence
options.c: Both held identical views on non-violence
options.d: Ambedkar held absolute non-violence as an end with relative violence as a means; Gandhi opposed violence of any kind without such distinction

faqs.a: Ambedkar held absolute non-violence as an end with relative violence as a means; Gandhi opposed violence of any kind without such distinction

faqs.q: Whose approach held that 'purity of means' determined the end, versus 'purity of ends' justifying the means?

options.c: Ambedkar held purity of means as key; Gandhi held purity of ends as justifying means
options.d: Gandhian perception held purity of means as key; Ambedkar held purity of ends as justifying means

faqs.a: Gandhian perception held purity of means as key; Ambedkar held purity of ends as justifying means

faqs.q: How did Ambedkar regard the untouchables, in contrast to Gandhi's view of them as an integral part of the Hindu whole?

options.b: As a religious minority, preferring to call them a 'political minority' or 'minority by force'

faqs.a: As a religious minority, preferring to call them a 'political minority' or 'minority by force'

faqs.q: What language did Gandhi typically speak in for mobilisation, compared to Ambedkar?

options.a: Gandhi spoke in English; Ambedkar spoke in vernacular
options.c: Gandhi spoke in plain local vernacular; Ambedkar spoke in English

faqs.a: Gandhi spoke in plain local vernacular; Ambedkar spoke in English

faqs.q: Which Gandhian principle had non-cooperation, hartal, satyagraha and civil disobedience as its outward manifestations, from which Ambedkar's approach differed?

options.a: To disobey the law in order to make the law more just
options.d: To rely exclusively on judicial appeals

faqs.a: To disobey the law in order to make the law more just
faqs.e: Ambedkar was more inclined toward observance of law and constitutionality in the political process.

faqs.q: How did Gandhi and Ambedkar differ in their preferred methods for solving the problem of untouchability?

options.b: Ambedkar favoured laws and constitutional methods; Gandhi treated it as a moral stigma to be erased through acts of atonement
options.c: Gandhi favoured legal methods; Ambedkar favoured moral atonement

faqs.a: Ambedkar favoured laws and constitutional methods; Gandhi treated it as a moral stigma to be erased through acts of atonement
